question.knowledge_point: Determining the Intervals of Concavity Given the Graph of the Second Derivative
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14032645/assets/305fa76994ff0be3c43894226eaa82d3d9e016c6add11cd48d80486c50643ed0.png)

The graph above shows $y={f}^{″}(x).$ Find the intervals on which the function $f(x)$ is concave down.
question.worked_solution:
A function $f(x)$ is concave down over an interval $(a,b)$ if ${f}^{″}(x)<0$ for all $x\in (a,b).$

On the given graph of $y={f}^{″}(x)$, we can see that ${f}^{″}(x)<0$ on the interval $(-4,-2)$ only. Therefore, the function $f(x)$ is concave down on the interval $(-4,-2)$ only.

evidence.solution_quote: Therefore, the function $f(x)$ is concave down on the interval $(-4,-2)$ only.

judgment.reasoning: All 16 selections agree with their own captured MA worked answers. Two explanations contain authored errors: q-2469 says statement VI where it means IV; q-114280 says the concavity changes from down to up at x=1 in its discussion of x=-1, but that change occurs at x=-1. These slips do not change MA's final selections. For q-114280, MA explicitly requires a tangent at an inflection point; under that convention only x=1 qualifies. A definition requiring continuity and a change of concavity without requiring a tangent would also admit x=-1, so that answer is convention-dependent. Mathematics: q-8186 and q-28524 use conjugate roots, producing 5x²+36=0 and -2x²-2=0. q-31228 has f''<0 only on (-4,-2); q-31214 has f''>0 only on (0,4). q-86174 has integral 5+(4-π)=9-π; the isolated value at x=3 does not affect it. q-11721 has determinant -3x, hence x=0. q-160619 applies -I, reversing the southwest vector to northeast; its selected image and MA's answer image show the same vector. q-160627 maps (a,b) to (b,-a), rotating clockwise by π/2; its selected image and MA's answer image show the same southeast vector. q-2469 has f''=12-24x, giving a minimum at 0 and a maximum at 1, so II and IV are true. Integration by parts gives the selected antiderivatives for q-78962 and q-114592; replacing -x with -(x-3) in the latter changes only the integration constant. q-156191 has an odd integrand, so the requested integral is -A. q-121517 intersects at -1 and 3/4, with upper-minus-lower equal to -8x²-2x+6. q-121585 has area integral from -2 to 2 of 8-2x², equal to 64/3. q-51428 changes concavity at x=1; x=3 has no concavity change and x=5 is undefined. No submitted-value grade evidence was supplied; every MA attribution below uses that question's captured worked solution.
